data.title: Novavax shareholder Shah Capital to step back from activist role
data.description:
Shah Capital, one of Novavax's top shareholders, said on Friday it no longer seeks to influence control of the vaccine maker after restructuring into a family office.

  • The investor has filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission to voluntarily withdraw its registration as an investment adviser, it said in a regulatory filing

  • Himanshu Shah Family Office LLC has been established to manage the investments, the filing said‌

  • Himanshu Shah is the founder, president and chief investment officer of Shah Capital, Novavax's second-largest shareholder, according to LSEG data

  • Shah Capital reported beneficial ownership of 10.54 million Novavax shares, or about 6.39% of the company

  • The filing also disclosed that Shah Capital Fund LLC sold 2.87 million shares on October 5 at an average price of about $11.35 apiece

  • Himanshu Shah reported beneficial ownership of 10.66 million shares, representing about 6.46% of Novavax

data.title: Kenvue loses bid for rehearing after Tylenol autism lawsuits revived
data.description:
By Diana Novak Jones

A US appeals court said on Friday it won’t reconsider a ruling reviving hundreds of lawsuits against Tylenol maker Kenvue alleging the popular painkiller can cause autism.

  • In a brief order, the 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals in Manhattan said it was rejecting a request from the company, which was spun off from Johnson & Johnson, to reconsider the three-judge panel’s ruling or to have the full court hear the case

  • In July, the panel revived about 500 lawsuits filed by parents over claims Tylenol use during pregnancy is linked to autism and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children

  • In that ruling, the court said a district court judge improperly excluded expert testimony from three doctors supporting the parents’ claims

  • Kenvue asked the court to reconsider the decision, saying district judges are the "true gatekeepers" who decide ⁠whether evidence is reliable enough to be admitted at trial

  • A spokesperson for Kenvue did not immediately respond to a request for comment

  • Friday’s ruling could pave the way for the company to appeal to the US Supreme Court

  • The issue drew greater attention after PresidentDonald Trump and top US health officials suggested a ​link to autism

  • There is no firm scientific evidence ​of a link between the drug and the conditions

data.title: Navigator Gas Announces Shareholder Meeting to Approve Change of Domicile to England and Wales
data.description:
LONDON, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Navigator Holdings Ltd. (described herein as “Navigator Gas” or the “Company”) announced today that, on October 8, 2026, it entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “Merger Agreement”) with its wholly owned English subsidiary, Navigator Gas plc (the “New Parent”), and Navigator Gas Merger Co Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of the New Parent (the “Merger Sub”).

Under the Merger Agreement, the Company will merge into the Merger Sub (the “Merger”), with Merger Sub continuing to exist as a wholly owned subsidiary of the New Parent, and each share of common stock of the Company (“Common Shares”) will be converted into one ordinary share of New Parent. As a result, the New Parent will become the publicly traded parent company of the Navigator group of companies and intends to list its ordinary shares on the NYSE under the existing “NVGS” ticker symbol.

The Merger Agreement was entered into in connection with the previously announced intention of the Company to change its corporate domicile from the Marshall Islands to England and Wales.

The change of corporate domicile is expected to bring Navigator’s corporate structure closer in line with its operating structure, with its executive office, senior management and many of its employees in the United Kingdom, along with lenders and insurers. The move is expected to give the Company the benefit of a well-developed legal and governance framework, a competitive and stable tax regime with an extensive double tax treaty network, as well as a mature and predictable tonnage tax regime for maritime businesses such as ours.

The closing of the Merger is subject to the conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, including the approval of the Merger by the affirmative vote of holders of at least a majority of the issued and outstanding Common Shares entitled to vote thereon. The Company does not expect the Merger to have a material impact on its employees, its day-to-day business and operations, or to services to its customers.

Mads Peter Zacho, Chief Executive Officer, said:

“The redomiciliation aligns the Company’s legal structure closely with where the business is managed and operated, as well as where many of our investors, lenders and insurers are based. It further supports our commitment to strong corporate governance and transparency, and provides a robust platform for future growth, investments, and strategic opportunities.”

The shareholders’ meeting to approve the Merger will be held at the offices of Baker Botts L.L.P., 30 Rockefeller Plaza, New York, New York 10112, U.S.A., at 9:00 a.m., U.S. Eastern Time, on November 16, 2026. A definitive proxy statement for the shareholders’ meeting was furnished to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) earlier today and is expected to be mailed on or about October 16, 2026, to all shareholders of Navigator Gas as of October 16, 2026, the record date for the shareholders’ meeting.

Notice of the shareholders’ meeting and the proxy statement are available on the Company’s website.

About Navigator Gas

Navigator Gas is the owner and operator of the world’s largest fleet of handysize liquefied gas carriers and a global leader in the seaborne transportation services of petrochemical gases, such as ethylene and ethane, liquefied petroleum gas and ammonia and owns a 50% share, through a joint venture, in an ethylene export marine terminal at Morgan’s Point, Texas on the Houston Ship Channel, USA. Navigator Gas’ fleet consists of 48 semi- or fully-refrigerated liquefied gas carriers, 18 of which are ethylene and ethane capable. The Company plays a vital role in the liquefied gas supply chain for energy companies, industrial consumers and commodity traders, with its sophisticated vessels providing an efficient and reliable ‘floating pipeline’ between the parties, connecting the world today, creating a sustainable tomorrow.

Navigator Gas’ Common Shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol “NVGS”.

PHILADELPHIA, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Iovance Biotherapeutics, Inc. ("Iovance" or the “Company”), a biotechnology company focused on innovating, developing, and delivering novel polyclonal tumor infiltrating lymphocyte (“TIL”) therapies for patients with cancer, today announced that on October 15, 2026 (the “Date of Grant”), the Company approved the grant of inducement stock options covering an aggregate of 111,615 shares of Iovance’s common stock to twenty-one new, non-executive employees.

The awards were granted under Iovance’s Amended and Restated 2021 Inducement Plan, which provides for the granting of equity awards to new employees of Iovance by the Company’s compensation committee in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4). Each of the stock options granted as referenced in this press release has an exercise price of $14.72, the closing price of Iovance’s common stock on the Date of Grant. Each stock option vests over a three-year period, with one-third of the shares vesting on the first anniversary of the employee’s start date (the “First Vesting Date”) and the remaining shares vesting in eight quarterly installments over the next two years, commencing with the first quarter following the First Vesting Date, subject to continued employment with the Company through the applicable vesting dates.

About Iovance Biotherapeutics, Inc.

Iovance Biotherapeutics, Inc. is the global leader in innovating, developing, and delivering tumor infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) cell therapies for patients with solid tumors. Amtagvi® (lifileucel) is the first FDA-approved, one-time treatment for previously treated advanced melanoma, now approved in three global markets and available at nearly 100 authorized treatment centers (ATCs). The Iovance TIL platform spans registrational trials and next-generation programs in additional solid tumors, including gene-edited and IL-12 tethered TIL therapies, next-generation IL-2, and precision immuno-oncology approaches. As the first and only company to take TIL therapy from concept to a broadly accessible commercial treatment, Iovance operates as an end-to-end cell therapy company, anchored by fully owned, centralized U.S.-based manufacturing that is scaled to serve thousands of cancer patients worldwide each year. Headquartered in Pennsylvania with offices and laboratories in California and Florida, Iovance serves patients at ATCs and clinical sites across almost the entire U.S. and in many countries around the world. data.title: Air-Traffic Controllers Reach Deal With FAA for 2.8% Pay Increase — WSJ
data.description:
By Andrew Tangel

Federal transportation officials struck a pay deal with the major union representing air-traffic controllers that aims to end a work practice that drew scrutiny after a deadly crash at New York's LaGuardia Airport earlier this year, according to people familiar with the matter.

Under the terms, the controllers would get a 2.8% pay increase. In exchange, they would also have to badge in and out of their air-traffic facilities. The deal is partly aimed at curtailing a longstanding practice of leaving work early known as an "early shove," the people said.

The early departures of controllers had emerged as a safety concern after a regional jet collided with a fire truck at LaGuardia airport last March, killing two pilots.

The Federal Aviation Administration, investigating the crash, found that two controllers had left the air-traffic tower before their shifts ended. The agency has moved to fire those and other controllers for what agency officials described as a form of timecard fraud.

The early shove, however, has been part of a longstanding, informal practice to allow air-traffic staff to leave early during less-busy times.

Controllers, members of the National Air Traffic Controllers Association, were slated to get a pay raise of 3.8% under a law that authorized the bump. The FAA gave them a 1% increase, but withheld the rest.

FAA chief Bryan Bedford has said he was authorized legally to withhold 2.8% of the increase as an incentive to get productivity gains from controllers.

The pay increase would take effect Oct. 18 and would be retroactive from the beginning of the year.

Also under the deal, FAA managers and union reps will hammer out new shift guidelines to maximize staffing during high traffic volumes. And facilities with the most severe staffing needs will get priority when controllers are reassigned to different locations.

The LaGuardia crash remains under investigation and it isn't clear what, if any, role air-traffic staffing may have played in the accident.

data.title: Top global climate science body suspends meeting without deal on major review timeline
data.description:
By Sudarshan Varadhan

A meeting of the members of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) was suspended without an agreement on a timeline to publish its next review of the latest science on the warming planet, the IPCC said on Friday.

The impasse over the timeline, which has lasted nearly three years, could leave countries to decide the next phase of climate action without consensus on critical issues, including the extent to which some global warming might be reversible.

The meeting was suspended after it ran over its planned duration on the last day and many delegations from least-developed countries and small island states had to leave, the IPCC said in a statement.

Agreeing publication dates for its next review of the latest science was the main agenda of the IPCC meeting of 195 member states in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa this week. Governments are set to assess progress toward goals set in the 2015 Paris agreement at the UN climate talks in November 2028, in a so-called "Global Stocktake".

The discussions on the review timeline and the IPCC budget "remain open," and the panel's deliberations will resume at the earliest opportunity, the IPCC said, without providing details.

The possibility that the IPCC's reports might not be ready in time for the 2028 climate talks has alarmed a coalition of 30 countries, including European, Latin American and small-island states pushing for immediate action.

However, countries including India, Kenya, Saudi Arabia, Russia and China are pressing for more time to prepare the IPCC's next reports to ensure scientists from less-resourced countries can make meaningful contributions.

"We were here to work, but found every proposal dismissed — on inclusivity, on the relevance of the science for our national planning, on the necessity of evidence to inform the next Global Stocktake," said Tina Stege, climate envoy for the Marshall Islands.

"Progress was blocked, down to the end — a shameful play for time when there is no time to waste."

The IPCC's reviews carry weight as they are written by hundreds of international experts and approved by every member state, and are used by governments to plan responses to climate change and cited in international court rulings.

The UN Environment Programme has said repeatedly that global efforts to limit warming are falling short and that deeper emissions cuts are needed to avoid climate-related disasters.

data.title: As AI rally wobbles, stock market's spotlight turns to earnings
data.description:
Key points:
  • Technology shares pull back after big run
  • AI trends in focus with results from Meta Platforms, chip companies
  • SpaceX, Tesla, Netflix among other reports due in coming week

By Lewis Krauskopf

Stumbles in the market-leading AI trade are set to test investor confidence in the rally in the coming week as Wall Street focuses on quarterly results due from key players including Meta Platforms .

AI-linked stocks, central to the bull market that just marked its fourth anniversary, struggled in recent days, with sharp declines in shares of semiconductor companies and tech hardware firms such as Dell Technologies .

Meta, among the hyperscalers spending massively to build AI data centers, highlights the upcoming week of quarterly reports, along with semiconductor firms Lam Research and Texas Instruments and Elon Musk-led companies SpaceX and Tesla .

"It certainly feels like the narrative in the market is a little bit jittery," said Garrett Melson, portfolio strategist with Natixis Investment Managers Solutions. "Clearly there's a lot of uncertainty around where AI stands right now."

Worries rippled through markets over risks tied to the financing of the AI build-out boom, which has lifted profits for a wide swath of companies and boosted economic growth. Investors were watching developments with CoreWeave , an AI cloud company with about $50 billion in debt. This week, its shares tumbled.

In other recent signs of caution, strategists at Deutsche Bank and RBC Capital Markets separately pulled back on their recommendations of the tech sector. On October 9, Deutsche Bank strategists said the rotation into tech had "run far and the risk-reward no longer looks favorable in the near term."

Dragged down by the swoon in heavyweight tech and AI stocks, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX posted its biggest weekly drop since June. But the benchmark index was only about 2% below its record high set this month. Other sectors, which lagged as tech shined last month, posted solid gains on the week, including healthcare and consumer staples.

"This is very much an on-off switch type of market," Melson said. "When AI is working, it sucks all the oxygen out of the room for the rest of the sectors."

META KICKS OFF HYPERSCALER RESULTS

US reporting season heats up next week, with investors counting on robust performance. S&P 500 companies are expected to have increased earnings by more than 30% in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES.

Massive outlays on AI data centers and infrastructure underpin the profit jump. Meta is one of five AI hyperscalers that combined are expected to increase their capital spending to about $1.2 trillion next year, according to Goldman Sachs. Investors are eager for signs the companies can show returns on the investments, which would build confidence that the spending is sustainable.

"One of the most important takeaways of earnings season is whether or not the profitability of the hyperscalers can grow faster than the pace of their capex," said Kevin Shea, senior equity analyst at BNY Wealth.

Shares of Meta, whose market capitalization was about $1.8 trillion, have risen in recent weeks as it launched its Muse AI assistant

"With the cost of capital going up, this capex blowout is going to become more expensive, which raises the bar for returns," said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services. "Meta is going to be the first up to try to provide some color around that question."

SEMIS, TESLA, NETFLIX ALSO ON TAP

Chip companies have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the capital spending boom, but the stocks have cooled off. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index has slumped about 12% this month, although it remained up 57% on the year, compared with a roughly 12% year-to-date gain for the S&P 500.

Wednesday's reports from Lam Research and Texas Instruments could offer broader indications of demand in the semiconductor industry. Lam Research shares are up 54% in 2026, while Texas Instruments stock is up 59%.

Elsewhere, investors will focus on results from Musk-run companies with market values well over $1 trillion: SpaceX — the newly public space company that also has an AI business — and Tesla, another signature stock of the tech-driven bull market.

Streaming company Netflix , consumer products company Procter & Gamble and engine maker GE Aerospace are among other high-profile reports in the coming week.

The rise in Treasury yields and prospects for further rate hikes from the Federal Reserve also remain front-burner issues for stock investors. Hot inflation data this week boosted bets on another rate increase at the Fed's meeting at the end of October. Futures pricing suggested most investors still expect the US central bank to wait until its meeting in December to raise rates for a second time this year.

"Another strong earnings season should help equities withstand moderately higher rates," analysts at UBS Global Wealth Management said in a note on Thursday.

data.title: Archimedes Tech SPAC Partners II Co. Announces Shareholder Approval of Proposed Business Combination with Forge Nano, Inc.
data.description:

(“Archimedes II” or “ATII”), a publicly traded special purpose acquisition company, today announced that at the Extraordinary General Meeting (the “Meeting”) held today, October 16, 2026, ATII’s shareholders voted to approve the previously announced business combination (the “Business Combination”) between ATII and Forge Nano, Inc. (“Forge Nano”), as well as all other proposals related to the Business Combination considered and voted upon at the Meeting.

The Business Combination is currently expected to close in the coming days, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of remaining closing conditions. Upon closing, the combined company (“Pubco”) is expected to operate as Forge Nano Holdings, Inc. and its shares of common stock and warrants are expected to trade on Nasdaq under the ticker symbols “NANO” and “NANOW,” respectively.

The results of the Meeting, as tabulated by an independent inspector of elections, will be included in a current report on Form 8-K to be filed by ATII with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”).

Archimedes II is a Cayman Islands exempted company led by Chairman Eric R. Ball and CEO Long Long and is comprised of technology investors, corporate-finance veterans, engineers, and SPAC specialists. Archimedes II was formed as a special-purpose acquisition company for the purpose of effecting a merger with one or more businesses in the technology industry. Archimedes II completed its $230 million IPO in February 2025, and its units, ordinary shares, and warrants currently trade on Nasdaq under the ticker symbols “ATIIU,” “ATII,” and “ATIIW,” respectively. About Forge Nano, Inc.

Forge Nano is a leading U.S.-based semiconductor equipment and advanced materials company pioneering Atomic Layer Deposition (“ALD”) technology for AI-era chip manufacturing and defense battery applications via its platform technology, Atomic Armor®. Atomic Armor® is a scalable, adaptable nano-scale coating system that strengthens America’s most critical systems – at the atomic level.   • The trade points to a small but growing use of prediction markets by businesses seeking protection against risks that conventional financial products may not cover

  • Kalshi platforms allow users worldwide to trade binary contracts on outcomes in politics, sports, economics and entertainment

US cash crude grades firmed on Friday, dealers said, as traders worried that escalating tensions in the Middle East could further tighten supplies.

A Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched towards the Red Sea city of Yanbu. The port is critical for Saudi Arabia's efforts to bypass the Strait of Hormuz and keep oil flowing to international markets.

Initial reports indicated no damage to Yanbu's infrastructure, consultants Rapidan Energy Group said.

"Israeli reports suggest Iran may be preparing a pre-emptive strike following unusual military movements detected by Western intelligence. Although unverified, these developments reinforce our view that persistent escalation risks will keep flat prices supported," Energy Aspects added.

Attacks around have also risen over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it was stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month.

The United States also issued a request for proposal for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels of crude oil from the nation's Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the Department of Energy said on Friday. The barrels will be a part of the last batch of oil, about 40 million barrels, that is yet to be released as part of the 172 million barrels of oil that the government agreed to release in March.
